results.label: this tree ships the M110 news-window module (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the app’s own calendar parser fed the rule: one synthetic release is in, one is out, and the parsed title/currency survive
a planned release 40 minutes in the FUTURE is not a blackout under a 15-minute block, even though a 45 would have caught it
a release 40 minutes AGO is a blackout under the 45-minute settle, labelled with the side that caught it
the blackout names the release, the elapsed time and the two configured numbers, and says the settle still has to pass
the payload echoes the pair it actually applied, so a caller never has to guess the window
the symbol’s currencies come from the app’s own mapping: a JPY release cannot block EURUSD
the recorded trap is now impossible: a 5-minute setting that silently collapsed the settle cannot clear a release that printed 10 minutes ago
and the fix is not over-blocking: a release 55 minutes ahead is clear under the 15-minute block
raising the BLOCK to 60 (his own option) catches the 55-minute-ahead release and leaves the settle at 45
with no note supplied the news row still describes how the test was shaped and names NO number
the account-sourced note replaces that fallback and names this account’s two numbers
with a blackout the row fails and its detail IS the blackout text, not a second wording of it
the blackout also lands in the no-trade veto list, and it is the engine’s own string
and it is a real veto: the blackout adds a blocking reason to the same bars that were clean a moment ago
the veto names both windows, so a NO TRADE can be audited against the settings that produced it
the boundaries are inclusive in the engine too: exactly 15 ahead and exactly 45 ago are each blocked on their own side
one minute outside either boundary is clear, so the window is never wider than it says
a news check is a read: every table is byte-identical afterwards
and it does not rewrite the account it read the pair from
M111’s feed really does fail here (the shim is refusing the URL, not serving an empty week)
M110 does not claim to fix M111: a failed calendar still reaches this rule as a QUIET one — blackout null and no unavailable flag
a failure is not cached the way a success is, so the next check retries the feed instead of freezing the outage
and the pair is still echoed on that path, so the outage can never be read as “45 minutes was applied and nothing was found”
the engine source keeps the M111 marker at that exact branch, so closing M111 later cannot be mistaken for a regression

scope: M110 engine: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock and a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser; two asymmetric news clocks, no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
